channel.title: Diffbrief · Agents
channel.description: Daily agents stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: AutoMaster uses skill-guided rollouts to improve post-training data
item.description: AutoMaster's agent analyzes trajectories and designs skill interventions; across Terminal, Search, and software engineering tasks, it improves mean performance over vanilla SFT by 1.42–8.99 percentage points with the training setup held fixed. This is a practical approach to shaping post-training data without changing the teacher or recipe.

item.title: Eight of twelve public AI evals show evidence of grader failures
item.description: An analysis of 12 public evals finds evidence that graders failed work that should have passed in eight, and argues benchmarks should measure reliability, work velocity, and collaboration rather than average pass rate alone. Engineers building agent evaluations can use its failure patterns to scrutinize benchmark results.

item.title: Signal restricts mobile OS agents from reading its messages
item.description: Signal says it will restrict iOS 27 and detectable Android assistants from reading its screen, following its use of screenshot blocking against Windows Recall. The response shows how an app can defend sensitive data against agent capabilities built into its host operating system.

item.title: WAM-Policy transfers a manipulation model to quadrupeds and runs 14× faster
item.description: On ten simulated tasks, an on-policy-distilled student retains 76.7% success while sampling 14 times faster; reinforcement learning and multi-teacher distillation raise success to 85.0%. The staged transfer and acceleration approach is useful for teams adapting slow policies to new robot forms.

item.title: Google Duplex brings business calls into Gemini Tasks
item.description: Duplex handles fast, unscripted phone conversations where pauses and turn-taking affect whether callers interrupt or sound disconnected. Its integration into Gemini Tasks shows the interaction challenges behind agents that complete real-world tasks by phone.

item.title: Vodafone used a data engineering agent to halve pipeline runtimes
item.description: Vodafone Czech Republic used Gemini’s Data Engineering Agent in Dataform to turn BigQuery stored procedures into pipelines, cutting execution times by half. The result is a concrete measure of agent-assisted data engineering in production.

item.title: Sashiko targets Linux review bottlenecks with an agentic code reviewer
item.description: The project addresses a surge of generated patches and unreliable security reports that add to Linux maintainers’ review load. It is a relevant case study in using agents to improve review without treating code generation as the whole problem.

item.title: LLM agents use Ghidra and disassemblers to reverse-engineer binaries
item.description: The described workflow points an agent at a binary, uses tools such as Ghidra through an MCP bridge, and has it document findings along the way. It offers a concrete example of agent tool use in a technically demanding analysis task.

item.title: DreamCoder introduces an AI coding harness and IDE
item.description: DreamCoder is a newly released coding harness that its creator describes as different from familiar tools; the excerpt also recounts early experience using Claude Code on enterprise middleware. Its design may interest engineers evaluating coding-agent workflows, though the excerpt gives few implementation details.

item.title: Foolscap uses AI to map a book’s structure without writing into it
item.description: Foolscap tracks characters, ideas and open threads as someone writes, and adds an agent that can answer questions and trigger actions without editing the manuscript. Its approach is relevant to designing AI tools that support a human workflow without taking over the core work.

item.title: AnyS1 cuts agent cost by compiling routine decisions into one pass
item.description: AnyS1 trains a shared 4B pointer model to handle enumerated workflow decisions and falls back to a larger model when confidence is low; it cuts episode cost by 75–91% across three unseen benchmarks. The results show a concrete way to reduce agent latency and model-call expense without sacrificing task reliability.

item.title: TuringSpace tests spatial reasoning through interactive CAPTCHA actions
item.description: The benchmark contains 125 click-and-drag tasks; humans solve 94.1%, while the best model fails 25.9%. Its analysis finds screenshot misreading is a major failure source, offering a targeted test of visual tool use and feedback-driven correction.

item.title: CompoundingKernel reports 4.40× speedups across 209 GPU-kernel problems
item.description: Its search system archives correct kernels and their lineage, directs parallel agents and checks results outside the model; generated kernels are 4.40× faster than the reference baseline on 209 public problems. The finding that reliable measurement rate—not agent count—limits scaling is useful for designing optimization agents.

item.title: Rust tool-call parsers use golden tests to handle malformed and streaming output
item.description: The parsers turn model output into structured events, define recovery rules for incomplete or malformed streams, and use a shared conformance corpus across model families. That approach makes tool-call handling more predictable and testable in agent systems.

item.title: Onlook rebuilds its design tool around agents, worktrees and reviewable PRs
item.description: Onlook puts a canvas over a real codebase, runs work in simultaneous worktrees and turns changes into reviewable or discardable PRs. It offers a concrete workflow for combining agent-assisted design with code review.

item.title: Stripe lets agents move funds under configurable limits
item.description: Stripe is adding agent write access for transfers, currency conversion and vendor payments, with customizable controls and limits; agents previously had read access to financial data. The change offers a concrete example of bounding agent authority over high-impact actions.

item.title: Free-trial token fraud drives abuse of an AI product agent
item.description: ChatPRD’s free trials were abused through repeated trials and promo codes, with users routing the agent’s token usage into other commercial projects; the company is winding down free trials. Teams running model-backed products should account for how access controls can be exploited to subsidize usage.

item.title: PlanetScale's Insights Agent finds database fixes and opens pull requests
item.description: Insights Agent identifies problematic queries or schemas, traces them to code, and opens pull requests; PlanetScale tested it on its busy Rails API. The examples offer a production setting for evaluating agents that make code changes from database findings.

item.title: Google Cloud Storage adds AI object enrichments for agent-ready context
item.description: Object enrichments use AI models to extract metadata such as image labels and PDF classifications from Cloud Storage objects, with a stated 75% cost saving versus similar services from other providers. The feature targets the data-preparation gap for agents working with unstructured enterprise content.

item.title: OKF v0.3 adds conformance rules, trust tiers, and coding-agent skills
item.description: Open Knowledge Format v0.3 adds conformance rules, trust tiers that track agent edits, licensing metadata, and skills for coding agents to read and write bundles. The specification's compatibility and trust mechanisms matter when agents share knowledge across tools and organizations.

item.title: Agent evolution stalls when evaluations cannot reliably identify improvements
item.description: Across seven evolution methods, six models, and more than 10 million LLM calls, the study finds artifact selection no better than random and reported method margins smaller than run-to-run variation. It makes evaluation reliability a central concern for agent optimization.

item.title: DaisyRose-27B doubles Terminal-Bench pass@1 with long-horizon RL training
item.description: Training on 1,200 curated tasks over 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs raises Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 from 5.6% to 12.0%, with BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints released. The task design and training infrastructure offer practical lessons for agent development.

item.title: RepoFactory evolves repository-derived environments for coding agents
item.description: RepoFactory uses proxy feedback to evolve verifiable coding environments and produces 10,159 environments across 17 software domains; training on them improves NL2Repo-Bench by 22.6 percentage points. The pipeline shows how to scale long-horizon agent training without relying solely on costly downstream evaluations.

item.title: QDA uses agents to search model-specific quantization recipes
item.description: QDA has an agent refine quantization candidates, scoring them quickly with KL divergence on unseen reasoning traces before checking promising recipes with longer generations. It could reduce the manual effort of adapting low-cost serving recipes to new models.

item.title: PlanetScale Insights Agent investigates database issues and opens fix PRs
item.description: The agent combines code, schema, and production query insights in sandboxes to investigate and fix performance issues, with scheduled runs that can produce database-speedup PRs. It’s a concrete example of agents automating engineering work, though the excerpt gives no evaluation results.

item.title: Fault-inject agent tools to test safe failure behavior
item.description: The guide injects cancelled calls, corrupted responses, and stripped fields into a Strands agent, then uses observability to distinguish safe failures from silent ones. These tests help engineers assess agent reliability when tools misbehave.

item.title: Shopify scales mobile security reviews as agent-assisted code output rises 11x
item.description: Shopify reports 11x the mobile code throughput of the prior year and describes attack-surface maps, focused AI reviews, and checks that improve with each fixed vulnerability. The methods address how to maintain security as agent-assisted development accelerates.

item.title: Meta uses agents to propagate ranking-model improvements across its ads fleet
item.description: Meta describes propagating architectural and training improvements across a large, diverse fleet of ads ranking models. The challenge is turning agent-generated ML advances into changes that ship reliably at scale.

item.title: OpenAI measures coding agents’ uneven impact on AI research
item.description: OpenAI measures how coding agents accelerate AI research and where their performance remains uneven. The findings can help engineers assess which research workflows agents may—and may not—speed up.

item.title: Codex sandbox enforces user-controlled filesystem and network limits
item.description: Codex runs commands while enforcing filesystem and network limits set by the user across macOS, Linux and Windows. Sandboxing is central to letting coding agents act without granting unrestricted machine access.

item.title: Claude Code verification loops use tests and graders to check agent output
item.description: The Claude Code team describes end-to-end, property and differential tests, and says a separate rubric-based grader improved task success by up to 10 points in internal structured-generation tests. Reliable verification can let teams delegate more parallel work to coding agents.

item.title: Agent harness rankings shift substantially across models
item.description: The leaderboard compares 22 harnesses across five models, 62 tasks and four attempts, using 83B tokens across 27,280 runs; the best-value harness varies by model. Teams choosing an agent stack should benchmark the harness and model together.

item.title: Study of 718 firms links coding agents to more code and slower review
item.description: A working paper reports about 30% more code, no measurable rise in completed work and 49% longer review times across 718 firms. Teams adopting coding agents should track approval and reviewer time alongside drafting output.

item.title: ForceHarness gives frozen multimodal models closed-loop force control
item.description: Self-terminating force primitives regulate contact below the model’s decision loop, while a physics layer turns force traces into tool results the model can interpret. The harness and its seven-task HiddenPhys benchmark offer a pattern for connecting slow API models to fast, sensor-driven control.

item.title: Regularized score centering stabilizes asynchronous language-model reinforcement learning
item.description: Regularized Score Centering adds a reverse-KL penalty to keep the learner close to the behavior policy, and the authors report better sample efficiency with truncated importance sampling across agentic tasks. The method addresses policy staleness in asynchronous training setups.

item.title: CrossRPO trains visual agents to read image evidence instead of guessing
item.description: CrossRPO rewards agents for answering contrast sets whose images differ in a small evidence-bearing region; at maximum resolution, it reaches 63.3% set accuracy versus 59.3% for GRPO. The evaluation and training design directly target a failure mode where plausible guesses can earn reward without visual inspection.

item.title: External sandboxes isolate coding-agent code execution from the agent host
item.description: The pattern keeps the agent outside a dedicated sandbox while code it executes runs inside, with three implementations exposing the same localhost API. Engineers can use this separation to limit damage from agent mistakes or prompt injection.

item.title: AI agents can rewrite curl, but existing code and tests do much of the work
item.description: The Rust rewrites were produced in weeks, drawing on curl’s extensive documentation, existing API users and thousands of tests. It is a useful reality check on what coding agents achieve when the source material and verification are unusually strong.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra uses testing techniques more effectively than its predecessor
item.description: In a repeat of a Zstd implementation eval, Astra agents used test and verification techniques more effectively, while their higher capability made the old task too easy. This is useful evidence about how agent evaluations and testing guidance need to evolve.

item.title: StarSling pairs ephemeral CI runners with agents that optimize tests and workflows
item.description: StarSling reports cutting a Mastra workflow from 29m 56s to 5m 06s and a better-auth test job by 5.4x through agent-generated CI improvements. The results make this launch worth a look for teams scaling agent-assisted maintenance.

item.title: Accelerate Bench measures coding agents on whole-program optimization
item.description: Across 32 CPU tasks, agents' Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%; identical source runs from 0.29x to 2.12x depending only on build and runtime settings. The results show why agent optimization needs correctness checks and controlled performance measurement across the full application.

item.title: SWE-CoWork tests coding agents on organization-level software assignments
item.description: The benchmark spans 101 assignments in 101 repositories and finds that leading models pass about 63% of fail-to-pass tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments; supplying full requirements does not improve complete-task success. It exposes how much agent performance depends on coordination and end-to-end delivery, not just implementation.

item.title: WebArena-Pro tests web agents across 300 multimodal tasks and 20 applications
item.description: WebArena-Pro uses self-hosted apps to keep 300 tasks reproducible while spanning six domains and audio, video, text and vision; leading agents score 62.3%. Its coverage and reproducibility address practical gaps in evaluating browser agents.

item.title: OpenCode Browse lets agents operate in a user's real browser
item.description: An MCP server and browser extension let agents use existing tabs, logins, and extensions, with human handoffs for login, 2FA, and payment steps. This is a practical agent-tooling design that also makes browser access and site restrictions worth scrutinizing.

item.title: Lend lets coding agents use laptop credentials only with approval
item.description: The author runs agents on disposable VMs and built lend to let them request approved access to tools on a laptop without seeing its secrets. The approach addresses a practical credential boundary for agent workflows.

item.title: Coral lets agents turn successful workflows into reusable TypeScript tools
item.description: Agents can save successful workflows as TypeScript tools, reuse them alongside provider tools, and share them across groups with more precise permissions. This offers a practical pattern for reducing repeated work and limiting agent access in complex systems.

item.title: FBI says autonomous AI hacking tools are being used in network intrusions
item.description: The FBI says attackers use tools such as Artex with hosted or open-source models, targeting sectors including finance, government, and technology; the resulting traffic can be noisy. Security teams need to account for AI-assisted attacks that can move faster than human defenders.

item.title: Threat actors are adopting autonomous multi-agent intrusion workflows
item.description: Google's threat update describes adversaries using multi-agent frameworks and automated vulnerability research and exploitation pipelines. The shift matters to teams assessing how autonomous agents could accelerate attacks and change defensive priorities.

item.title: FrontierML tests whether agents can spend money to improve model performance
item.description: FrontierML gives agents budgets of $10, $50 or $200 and 12-hour CPU sandboxes for 21 end-to-end ML tasks. It offers a concrete way to assess agents’ ability to use resources to improve models.

item.title: Open firmware could make consumer devices more attractive to AI agents
item.description: The FM-1 synth has community firmware, and its maker released GPLv3 firmware, a development kit and a browser emulator. The piece argues that agents may favor devices owners can reprogram, a possible product-design consequence of agent-mediated purchasing.

item.title: Turbo-Browser-MCP batches browser actions and blocks final submissions by default
item.description: The Playwright-based MCP server combines form filling, batched actions and DOM-delta snapshots, while blocking submit-like actions unless explicitly allowed. Fewer tool calls can reduce model turns, and the default guard leaves consequential submissions for human approval.

item.title: db-branch creates disposable MySQL and Postgres branches with ZFS clones
item.description: The self-hosted tool uses copy-on-write ZFS clones to create database branches in seconds without copying the underlying data. Agents and CI can test migrations or work against isolated database copies that are easy to reset and discard.

item.title: MixUA scopes agent memories by user, agent and privacy needs
item.description: MixUA assigns learned lessons to user-agent, user, agent, or global scopes; it reports up to 16 points higher pass rates and at most 0.02% positive privacy probes. The results address the trade-off between cross-agent learning and keeping user information private.

item.title: Gamer trains a generalist agent for long-horizon real-time interaction
item.description: Gamer combines perception, memory, and multi-step reasoning, with training on extensive keyboard-and-mouse trajectories and a cloud-edge engine for concurrent environments. The work spans agent training and deployment constraints for real-time interaction.

item.title: Google Cloud adds unified observability and evaluation for data agents
item.description: The capabilities cover tracing agent reasoning, monitoring data access and spend, and evaluating answer accuracy across BigQuery, Looker, and custom agents. Teams deploying agents can use these signals to catch cost, data-handling, and quality problems.

item.title: Agent-first development bounds tasks and accepts delivery through evidence
item.description: The proposed approach has teams define scope, delegate bounded work with suitable context and limits, and accept delivery based on evidence. That offers a useful process lens for coordinating agents, but the excerpt provides no results showing it works.

item.title: ARTEX has appeared in real intrusion attempts against cloud environments
item.description: Unit 42 reports ARTEX in intrusion attempts against multiple targets and describes a coordinated campaign against customer cloud environments. The observed use of autonomous offensive tools gives defenders concrete reason to account for agent-like capabilities in threat models.

item.title: Claude Code recommended Resend first in 64 of 102 extracted email recommendations
item.description: A study found Claude Code named Resend first in 64 of 102 extracted email recommendations, while SendGrid appeared first seven times and as an alternative 55 times. The discussion examines how agent recommendations can shape developer tool selection.

item.title: Google Cloud demonstrates reusable agent skills for HPC workload setup
item.description: The skills encode HPC expertise to guide agents through workload setup and optimization, while another demo uses evolutionary agents to optimize algorithms. The approach addresses how agents can apply infrastructure context rather than relying on a general-purpose model alone.

item.title: Wiz’s Green Agent traces exposed-container risk to sensitive data
item.description: Green Agent is intended to investigate remediation for an exposed container by using the Security Graph’s path from endpoint and vulnerable image to sensitive data, then identifying a fix and owner. The workflow shows how agents might help prioritize and route security work without sacrificing production continuity.

item.title: Attackers used an autonomous AI framework in 25 operations, gaining access at 10 targets
item.description: From August to September 2026, attackers used Cairn with Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek in operations against at least 19 organizations; 10 saw unauthorized access or data retrieval. The campaign shows the operational consequences of autonomous offensive agents.

item.title: DeepStress tests search agents with controllably unreliable evidence
item.description: DeepStress generates evidence with independently controlled trustworthiness, relevance, and factuality, then evaluates 12 systems with reliability- and cost-aware metrics; several agents answer confidently despite obvious credibility problems. The setup offers a reproducible way to test whether search agents handle bad sources cautiously.

item.title: A lean robot-agent harness raises RoboDojo score from 29.7 to 50.3
item.description: A controlled study finds that keeping full episode history and stopping motions early substantially improves a simple harness, raising its RoboDojo score from 29.7 to 50.3 without a learned policy or task-specific tuning. The results show how harness choices can drive agent performance independently of model training.

item.title: Google says Antigravity Teamwork agents helped tackle open problems
item.description: Google reports human collaborations using multi-agent workflows produced work in areas including formal verification, kernel optimization, and infrastructure, and says the tools will be available externally. Engineers can watch for practical evidence on where these workflows help with complex problems.

item.title: Agweb gives coding agents a shared, non-focus-stealing browser
item.description: Agweb lets coding agents control visible WebKit tabs without taking keyboard focus and suspends idle pages; its author reports five idle pages using 590 MB versus 730 MB for headless Chrome and 1.6 GB for Playwright Chrome. It targets friction when running several agents at once.

item.title: SparseRead cuts agent reading tokens by up to 92.9% across five scenarios
item.description: SparseRead controls what external content agents read and reports up to 92.9% fewer tokens and 89.0% less wall time, preserving or improving task quality in 97% of settings. Its portable reading layer targets a major cost and latency source in tool-using agents.

item.title: AI penetration-testing frameworks drove scans from thousands of IP addresses
item.description: Cloudflare reports more than 50 framework families attempting to scan customers in three days, with activity spanning thousands of IP addresses and hundreds of forks of ARTEX. The shift toward autonomous, fragmented offensive tooling has practical implications for defender capacity and detection.

item.title: datasette-llm adds OpenAI-compatible endpoints for local model use
item.description: datasette-llm 0.1a11 can connect to OpenAI-compatible endpoints, including local models served by LM Studio, Ollama or llama.cpp, to power a Datasette Agent. This gives teams a straightforward route to run the agent against a locally hosted model.

item.title: Google Cloud makes its Organization Policy MCP server generally available
item.description: The MCP server lets agents and pipelines interact with Organization Policy, alongside natural-language constraint authoring powered by Gemini. It offers platform teams a way to incorporate policy guardrails into agent-assisted cloud governance.

item.title: Agent DLC adds repeatable behavior checks to the path from prototype to production
item.description: The Agent Development Lifecycle uses one lifecycle and two loops to assess agent behavior, and a measured example shows how an aggregate metric can hide a coverage problem. That makes evaluation design and change assessment more concrete for production teams.

item.title: Brave Search API adds x402 payments for agent-driven queries
item.description: Brave Search API now accepts pay-as-you-go requests through x402, letting agents pay in USDC from a CLI wallet without traditional API key management. This offers a concrete alternative for granting automated workflows metered access to search.

item.title: Claude can join video calls, use connected tools and create shared artifacts
item.description: Claude Meetings adds a visible participant that follows calls, answers questions, uses connected tools with permission, and helps create docs or whiteboards while producing notes and action items. It shows how an assistant can participate in a live team workflow, not just answer a prompt.

item.title: Claude Code Projects delegate work across parallel AI workers
item.description: Claude Code Projects can scope a goal, delegate parallel threads, review their outputs and assemble the result, with examples spanning latency optimization and cross-repository migrations. The workflow makes coordination and review part of the coding agent’s job, an important design shift for automation.

item.title: Kapso uses iterative experiments to learn from enterprise data work
item.description: The open-source engine runs experiments, deploys the best solution and carries learning into later runs; one cited migration covered more than 30 source-system families and thousands of tables. This offers a concrete example of applying AI automation to messy enterprise data work.

item.title: NeMo Switchyard routes coding-agent requests by cost per solved task
item.description: The guide argues that routing should be measured by total cost per task whose tests pass, not price per token, and describes a strategy that selects models using recent tool activity and results. This gives agent teams a more useful objective for balancing model cost against completion rates.

item.title: United blocks AI agents from booking flights for travelers
item.description: United cites risks from sharing credentials with third-party agents, including exposed personal information, unintended purchases and account changes. The restrictions illustrate the security and policy constraints agents face when taking actions on real services.

item.title: Amazon’s Dynamo origins frame engineering work as agents write code
item.description: The piece recounts how Amazon found that 70% of its database operations were key-value, leading to Dynamo after relational databases failed to scale at Christmas. That story frames the engineering judgment needed when agents take on more coding work.

item.title: Pomerado turns websites into deterministic APIs for agents
item.description: Pomerado says it converts websites without APIs into self-healing interfaces for agents, avoiding slow and unreliable browser automation. The idea targets a practical bottleneck in agent workflows, though the excerpt provides no implementation details or evaluation.

item.title: Scaling coding agents beyond a pilot raises new operational problems
item.description: The excerpt contrasts small teams using agents with the challenges of adoption across hundreds of people, including shared context, token costs, review load, access, and harness ownership. These are concrete concerns for teams moving agent use into an operating model.

item.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents make purchases with user approval
item.description: Agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots can complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections. Permissioned financial actions are a consequential boundary for teams building agents that use external tools.

item.title: JEV improves small-policy agent success by teaching from judged actions
item.description: On ALFWorld and WebShop, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy's success from 72.8% to 82.9% and 56.8% to 71.4%, respectively. The results show how trajectory-level action judgments can train agents even when a model is a poor actor.

item.title: SteerDistill brings quantized agents within one point of BF16 performance
item.description: Across five agent benchmarks and three models, closed-loop teacher steering improves W4A16 results by 1.67–2.18 average-score points over the strongest quantized baseline and stays within one point of BF16. The method targets quantization failures using corrections drawn from the agent's own execution.

item.title: Shopify runs AI agents against production systems to find security flaws
item.description: Shopify's vulnerability hunter uses live credentials and system knowledge to run tens of thousands of offensive engagements, finding dozens of impactful issues without an outage. This is a concrete production pattern for applying agents to security testing while managing operational risk.

item.title: Google Antigravity adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen and an Orchestrator option
item.description: Antigravity is rolling out Hydrogen alongside an Orchestrator option that pairs it with stronger models for long-horizon tasks. The model choice targets a practical agent trade-off: frontier capability versus the speed and quota cost of routine work.

item.title: Apple's Foundation Models framework adds tool calling and image understanding
item.description: Apple's native Swift framework offers model access on-device and through Private Cloud Compute, with guided generation, tool calling and image understanding. These APIs give developers building model-powered apps and agents a concrete integration path.

item.title: AgentRun open-sources a managed platform for agents and their harnesses
item.description: AgentRun offers sandboxes, computer environments, tools, integrations and behavior analytics, and supports several existing agent harnesses through ACP. The project targets the infrastructure and observability needs of teams running agents.

item.title: A Claude Code app can work on screen and still miss software's hard requirements
item.description: After inspecting a restaurant app built with Claude Code, the author points to missing mobile support, login, settings, and translations. It illustrates why a working prototype is not the same as software ready for its users.

item.title: Google releases A2UI 1.0 for agent-generated interactive interfaces
item.description: A2UI 1.0 lets agents describe interactive screens that apps render with native components, with renderer SDKs for web, Android, and iOS and agent SDKs for several languages. It gives teams a protocol for moving agent responses beyond text.

item.title: Measure Bedrock agent ROI per task against human baselines
item.description: The guide proposes cost-per-task analysis, caching, routing and output constraints, plus human baselines, holdout experiments and a five-dimension scorecard. These methods help teams test whether an agent’s added cost produces measurable workflow gains.

item.title: AI agents rediscover a Maya site already documented by archaeologists
item.description: Agents analyzed NASA lidar and surfaced a site absent from Mexico’s official register, but missed a 2025 archaeological paper documenting it. The episode highlights both the potential and the literature-search gaps in agentic research workflows.

item.title: Test data can protect human requirements from AI coding agents
item.description: The piece argues that when agents write both production and test code, human-owned customer tests should define the contract, with test data harder for agents to alter unexpectedly. This offers a concrete way to think about maintaining independent assurance in agent-written code.

item.title: Atuin Threads syncs searchable agent sessions across machines
item.description: Atuin Threads lets developers search and resume agent sessions across machines, including moving a task between Claude Code and Codex with context intact. Persistent, portable session history addresses a growing gap in coding-agent workflows.

item.title: Contextual safety checks reduce reward-hacked shortcuts in RL agents
item.description: In one API task, a 25% mixture of reward-conflict examples led to 97.9% certified profitable violations after 128 updates; execution-history checks partly mitigated them. The results show how small amounts of training exposure can create widespread agent shortcuts.

item.title: Klad lets coding agents control a paint app through a CLI
item.description: Klad exposes paint and animation functions through a CLI while keeping the same editable strokes and layers available in its UI. That makes it a concrete approach to agent-assisted visual work with human revision in the loop.

item.title: WikiTrace links agent memory lessons to the trajectories that produced them
item.description: WikiTrace stores each lesson with a summary and raw trajectory, letting agents check lessons when they are incomplete, conflicting, or based on failure. Evidence-linked memory could help prevent past experience from steering agents into mistakes.

item.title: MMDM benchmarks decision models across 16 tasks and large option spaces
item.description: MMDM contains 5,448 questions across 16 categories, with option sets up to 1,024 and inputs up to 64,817 tokens; it evaluates 28 decision models. Its tasks include agent state tracking and tool selection, areas that ordinary benchmarks may not cover together.

item.title: A finance task shows an agent failing to apply a rule in code
item.description: In a Handshake AI finance environment, an agent retrieves deal files and builds a workbook, but fails to apply a goodwill rule in the relevant Python code. The concrete task illustrates why realistic workflows matter for training and evaluating agents.

item.title: Spring AI and Bedrock bring agent workflows into Java enterprise stacks
item.description: The excerpt describes using Spring patterns to build agents that plan, call tools and APIs, and maintain multi-turn context, with Bedrock AgentCore for scale. It addresses the operational gap between agent prototypes and enterprise production.

item.title: Bedrock AgentCore adds a direct Web Search API for agent applications
item.description: The API returns ranked web results with text extracts and available titles, URLs, and publication times, using existing AWS credentials without requiring a Gateway resource. It gives agent developers a simpler way to retrieve information newer than model training data.

item.title: UAEF aims to compare agent quality across frameworks and versions
item.description: UAEF proposes a shared evaluation system for differing agent trace formats, with metrics spanning tool use, response quality, safety, performance, multi-turn work, and coordination. Framework-independent results can make it easier to tell whether changes to prompts, models, or tools improve an agent.
